THE BOURNE IDENTITY (2002)
DETAILED SCREENPLAY-STYLE RETELLING
ORIGINAL RETELLING — NOT THE ORIGINAL SCREENPLAY

NOTE: This is an original, scene-oriented retelling of the film's story. It does not reproduce the copyrighted screenplay or dialogue.

========================================
ACT I — THE MAN WITHOUT A NAME
========================================

FADE IN:

EXT. MEDITERRANEAN SEA — NIGHT

Dark water stretches beneath a moonless sky. A fishing vessel cuts through the waves.

The crew spots something in the water.

They pull an unconscious MAN aboard.

INT. FISHING VESSEL — LATER

The man slowly wakes. He is injured and disoriented.

He searches his memory.

Nothing.

He does not know his name. He does not know where he came from. He does not know why he was floating in the sea.

A fisherman discovers a tiny device associated with the man's body. It contains a bank account number in Zurich.

The stranger studies the information.

It is the first clue to a life he cannot remember.

CUT TO:

EXT. ZURICH — DAY

The stranger travels to Switzerland.

He enters a bank and accesses a safety-deposit box.

Inside are passports, money, and documents bearing several different names.

He examines them one after another.

Each name appears to belong to him.

None of them feels familiar.

He takes the passports and money.

Now he has identities, but no identity.

EXT. ZURICH STREET — DAY

He walks through the city.

Something about the environment feels strangely familiar.

He notices exits.

He notices surveillance.

He instinctively evaluates strangers around him.

He realizes that he possesses abilities he cannot explain.

Someone nearby appears to be watching him.

The stranger moves.

The watcher moves too.

The stranger understands that his mysterious past is not merely a puzzle.

Someone is looking for him.

EXT. ZURICH — LATER

He meets MARIE, a young woman preparing to travel.

He offers her money if she will drive him to Paris.

She agrees.

They leave together.

INT. CAR — DAY

Marie drives.

The stranger studies the passports and tries to understand the person behind them.

Marie asks questions.

He has few answers.

His uncertainty is genuine.

He is not pretending to have lost his memory.

He really does not know who he is.

EXT. PARIS — DAY

They arrive.

The stranger begins following the clues contained in his documents.

He discovers that one of his identities is connected to a Paris address.

He goes there.

The place offers another fragment of his past.

But it also confirms something frightening:

His former life involved secrecy and violence.

CUT TO:

EXT. PARIS STREET — DAY

A man approaches him.

The stranger recognizes the danger before he consciously understands why.

He escapes.

The escape is remarkably efficient.

He uses his surroundings, timing, and physical ability with almost no hesitation.

Afterward, he is shaken.

He realizes his body remembers things his mind does not.

CUT TO BLACK.

========================================
ACT II — THE PAST HUNTING HIM
========================================

INT. PARIS APARTMENT — DAY

Bourne investigates the identities he discovered.

Documents and photographs begin forming a picture.

He learns that he was connected to a covert intelligence operation.

The truth is worse than he expected.

He was not simply a man who happened to possess several passports.

He was a trained operative.

His skills, reflexes, and ability to disappear were learned for a purpose.

EXT. PARIS — VARIOUS LOCATIONS — DAY/NIGHT

Bourne moves through the city with Marie.

They become increasingly close.

Marie sees that he is frightened by what he is discovering.

He is not afraid of physical danger alone.

He is afraid of the person he may have been.

INT. HOTEL — NIGHT

Bourne examines his weapons and documents.

Memories begin returning in fragments.

He remembers an assignment.

He remembers a target.

He remembers failure.

The pieces suggest that he had been sent to eliminate a powerful African dictator.

The operation went wrong.

The failed mission appears to have triggered the chain of events that left Bourne in the sea.

Bourne realizes that his old employers are still searching for him.

EXT. PARIS — DAY

Agents continue trying to locate him.

Bourne stays ahead of them.

Each confrontation reveals another part of his training.

But each victory also makes him more uncomfortable.

He does not want to become the man his training created.

INT. MARIE'S FAMILY HOME — DAY

Marie allows Bourne to stay temporarily.

The contrast is striking.

For the first time, he experiences something resembling an ordinary life.

He sees a world that exists outside surveillance, missions, aliases, and violence.

He begins imagining that another life might be possible.

CUT TO:

INT. INTELLIGENCE OFFICE — DAY

The officials tracking Bourne discuss the situation.

The missing operative has become a problem.

The people responsible for him want him located.

Bourne, meanwhile, is making a decision.

He will not return.

EXT. EUROPEAN CITY — DAY

Bourne continues moving.

He discovers the location of another operative connected to his former organization.

The encounter forces him to confront what his old life did to people.

Bourne has an opportunity to kill.

He chooses not to.

Instead, he leaves.

This is an important change.

He is no longer simply surviving.

He is choosing what kind of person he wants to be.

INT. PARIS HOTEL — NIGHT

Bourne tells Marie that he cannot keep running forever.

He wants freedom.

But freedom requires leaving behind the identity that made him dangerous.

He prepares for one final confrontation with the people connected to his past.

========================================
ACT III — WALKING AWAY
========================================

EXT. PARIS — DAY

Bourne confronts people connected to the operation.

He uses his intelligence and training to stay alive.

But he refuses to return to the organization.

His former life is losing its hold over him.

INT. INTELLIGENCE OFFICE — DAY

The officials realize that Bourne is no longer controllable.

He has disappeared.

The pursuit begins to collapse.

EXT. PARIS — DAY

Bourne meets Marie.

There is a sense that the chase is finally over.

He has learned enough about himself to understand one thing:

He cannot change everything he did in his former life.

But he can choose what he does next.

FADE TO:

EXT. GREECE — DAY

Bourne begins living quietly.

He has abandoned the identities that once defined him.

He starts building an ordinary existence.

The man who began the film asking, "Who am I?" no longer needs the answer from his old documents.

He is creating a new identity through his choices.

FADE OUT.

========================================
STRUCTURAL LESSON
========================================

Ordinary/unknown protagonist
        ↓
Mysterious clues
        ↓
Discovery of a hidden past
        ↓
Realization that someone is hunting him
        ↓
Repeated escapes
        ↓
Investigation into his former identity
        ↓
Moral choice
        ↓
Break from the organization
        ↓
New life
